relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: In 1911, he enrolled at the Tsinghua School, where he graduated in 1916.

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: Tang arrived in the United States in 1918 at the age of 25 to begin his education at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts. He returned to China after graduation in 1922

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: that same year became professor of National Southeast University.

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: After a short period of teaching students in Nankai University

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: he returned to Nanjing, where he was a professor at National Central University.

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.role: professor at the Department of Philosophy
relations.evidence: In 1931, he moved to Peking University as a professor at the Department of Philosophy, where he was promoted to dean of College of Liberal Arts in 1946.

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: In the following 1947 he went to the University of California, Berkeley, where he lectured the History of Chinese Buddhism.

relations.subject: Tang Yongtong
relations.evidence: He was appointed vice-president of Peking University in 1951.

relations.subject: Tang Yijie
relations.evidence: Their elder son, Tang Yijie (1927–2014), was a Peking University professor

relations.subject: Tang Yijie
relations.evidence: The couple had two sons and two daughters, in order of birth: Tang Yimei (湯一梅; died young), Tang Yijie (湯一介), Tang Yixuan (湯一玄) and Tang Yiping (湯一平).
